title: Edge regional traffic fencing for stream-consistent active-active routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: In our active-active hosted API topology, long-lived streaming sessions and session-affine requests can see inconsistent behavior during partial region degradation or noisy neighbors. Current region failover approaches either cause session breakage (hard failover) or complexity (sticky routing) and do not combine SLO-preserving load shedding with graceful routing changes. This ticket designs and implements a regional traffic fencing pattern that: 1) maintains stream/session continuity where possible, 2) enables incremental traffic fencing between regions, 3) integrates circuit breaker signals and backpressure-aware load shedding, and 4) produces telemetry to validate end-to-end SLO impact.
acceptance_criteria: Can perform a staged traffic fence operation between two regions without dropping active streams for >= 99% of sessions in a canary at 5% traffic
Circuit breaker signals (latency / error / queue depth) propagate to routing layer within 2s and trigger fencing decisions documented in runbooks
Load shedding policy reduces downstream p99 latency by at least 30% under oversubscription while maintaining p50 within 10% of baseline
Metrics (per-session continuity, reattach rate, token-level latency, failed reconnects) are emitted to Console dashboards and match expected thresholds in test harness
Automated e2e test simulates region partial outage and verifies graceful fencing with session-aware retries in SDKs
Rollout plan executed to shift 50% of traffic to fenced behavior in a single cluster without customer-reported disruptions
design_notes: Introduce 'regional fence' state in gateway routing table: OPEN, FENCING, FENCED, ROLLBACK
Fencing is initiated by routing controller based on composite health scores from region telemetry (latency, error-rate, capacity). Controller emits a staged plan with per-route fences

Streaming sessions carry deterministic session affinity token (session_id + region_hash). During FENCING, gateways accept new streams only if the session affinity matches target rules; existing streams are allowed to finish or be offered graceful reattach via SDK helper
Circuit breakers at runtime level will expose aggregate signals and severity tags (soft, hard). Soft opens trigger load-shedding hints; hard opens initiate immediate fencing for non-critical routes

Load shedding uses four levers: deny-new-streams, degrade-response (lower tokens or reduced payloads), queuing limit per-worker, and preemptive rejection based on client tier. Policies are configurable per-customer and per-route
Telemetry schema will include 'fence_id', 'fence_phase', 'session_continuity', 'reattach_attempts', and 'shed_reason' labels for downstream analysis
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Controller changes - implement fence state machine and composite health scorer (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Gateway changes - accept fence directives, implement per-session acceptance checks and graceful stream termination API (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Runtime changes - emit circuit breaker severity and queue-depth metrics; plumb shedding hints into request admission (2 weeks)
Phase 4: SDK + Client helpers - implement reattach semantics and user-visible retry guidance (1 week)
Phase 5: Telemetry & dashboards - Console panels for fence ops and per-route SLO impact (1 week)
Phase 6: Testing & e2e - fault injection in staging across AZ/region, runchaos tests and traffic replay (2 weeks)
Phase 7: Canary rollout - 5% -> 20% -> 50% fences with operator checklists (1 week)
risks: Incorrect fence decision could cause cross-region request amplification if controllers oscillate; mitigate with hysteresis and backoff windows
SDK reattach may not be adopted immediately by clients leading to more reconnects than expected; mitigation: server-side reattach tokens and conservative default reattach timeouts
Telem gaps: if gateway lacks per-session ids in some routes, continuity measurement will be incomplete; mitigate by requiring session tagging for streaming endpoints before fencing is enabled
Load shedding incorrectly configured could cause disproportionate impact to low-tier customers; require per-customer policy and simulation prior to rollout
testing_plan: Unit tests for fence state machine and controller decision logic
Integration tests between controller and gateway with mocked circuit-breaker signals
Staging chaos tests: simulate region degradation (CPU/GPU saturation, disk/network flaps) and validate fencing progression
Load test with synthetic long-lived streams to measure reattach and continuity metrics under fence scenarios
SLO regression harness: baseline and post-change comparison for p50/p90/p99 latency and error rates
User acceptance: run with internal customers (billing, search) and collect feedback during 5% canary
rollout_strategy: Start with internal-only routes and a feature flag controlled fence controller
Enable fencing in passive mode (controller suggests moves but does not enforce) for 48h to collect telemetry
Canary phase: enable enforcement for 5% traffic with ~30 minute operator observation windows
Progressively increase to 20% and 50% with automated rollback on threshold breaches (high reattach rate, >2% session loss, or SLO degradation)
Full enable only after two successful 50% canary cycles and documented runbook updates
